`date`: print the date and time.

## Synopsis

<strong>date</strong> \[<em>+FORMAT</em>\]

## Description

<strong>date</strong> prints the date and time by the board's real-time clock, which keeps the world's time: the clock files on disks are stamped with.

Dates are the world's calendar: days are numbered from 1, and a day has 24 of the game's hours, as Minecraft counts them, so 06:00 is sunrise and 18:00 sunset. The first day's sunrise is the epoch. A day of the world is 20 minutes of real time.

With no <em>FORMAT</em>, it prints <strong>Day 3 14:05:09</strong>.

## Options

<strong>+</strong><em>FORMAT</em>
: What to print, as <strong>os.date</strong> formats it: <strong>%d</strong> the day, <strong>%H</strong> <strong>%M</strong> <strong>%S</strong> the hour, minute and second, <strong>%T</strong> all three, <strong>%R</strong> hours and minutes, <strong>%s</strong> seconds since the epoch, <strong>%c</strong> the default, <strong>%%</strong> a percent sign.

## Exit status

0 when it printed; 1 for a format it does not know.

## Examples

```text
date
date +%H:%M
date +%s
```

## Notes

GNU <strong>date</strong> prints the Gregorian calendar's date, and can set the clock (<strong>-s</strong>); mcos's world has no months or years, and its clock is the world's, which no program sets.

## See also

<strong>uptime</strong>(1)
